title: 1Password app data
whyItMatters: 1Password keeps its local database, settings and account state here. It shows the app was used on this computer and may hold account metadata even while the vault is locked.
source: 1Password Support, How to uninstall 1Password: Linux data under ~/.config/1Password - https://support.1password.com/uninstall-1password/
notes: The encrypted database and settings live in this folder. Nothing is opened or decrypted. Flatpak installs may keep a sandboxed copy under their own app data.

cleanup.exportFirst: Confirm you can sign in to your 1Password account, have the Secret Key and Emergency Kit, and export any vault you need.
cleanup.signOut: Sign out of 1Password on this computer and remove this device from the authorized devices in your account settings.
steps: Confirm the account sign-in details and Emergency Kit are available.
Export the vaults you need and check that the export opens.
Sign out of 1Password and remove this device from the account.
If you decide to remove the app, uninstall 1Password from your software manager.
Delete the 1Password folder named in the plan only after the export is confirmed.
cleanup.risk: Removes the local 1Password database and settings from this computer. Items that are only in the account stay in the cloud.
